"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/time-to-cross-a-bridge/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

2532. Time to Cross a Bridge

There are k workers who want to move n boxes from the right (old) warehouse to the left (new) warehouse. You are given the two integers n and k, and a 2D integer array time of size k x 4 where time[i] = [right_i, pick_i, left_i, put_i].

The warehouses are separated by a river and connected by a bridge. Initially, all k workers are waiting on the left side of the bridge. To move the boxes, the i-th worker can do the following:

- Cross the bridge to the right side in right_i minutes.
- Pick a box from the right warehouse in pick_i minutes.
- Cross the bridge to the left side in left_i minutes.
- Put the box into the left warehouse in put_i minutes.

The i-th worker is less efficient than the j-th worker if either condition is met:
- left_i + right_i > left_j + right_j
- left_i + right_i == left_j + right_j and i > j

The following rules regulate the movement of the workers through the bridge:
- Only one worker can use the bridge at a time.
- When the bridge is unused prioritize the least efficient worker (who have picked up the box) on the right side to cross. If not, prioritize the least efficient worker on the left side to cross.
- If enough workers have already been dispatched from the left side to pick up all the remaining boxes, no more workers will be sent from the left side.

Return the elapsed minutes at which the last box reaches the left side of the bridge.

Example 1:

Input: n = 1, k = 3, time = [[1,1,2,1],[1,1,3,1],[1,1,4,1]]
Output: 6
Explanation:
From 0 to 1 minutes: worker 2 crosses the bridge to the right.
From 1 to 2 minutes: worker 2 picks up a box from the right warehouse.
From 2 to 6 minutes: worker 2 crosses the bridge to the left.
From 6 to 7 minutes: worker 2 puts a box at the left warehouse.
The whole process ends after 7 minutes. We return 6 because the problem asks for the instance of time at which the last worker reaches the left side of the bridge.

Example 2:

Input: n = 3, k = 2, time = [[1,5,1,8],[10,10,10,10]]
Output: 37
Explanation:
The last box reaches the left side at 37 seconds. Notice, how we do not put the last boxes down, as that would take more time, and they are already on the left with the workers.

Constraints:

    1 <= n, k <= 10^4
    time.length == k
    time[i].length == 4
    1 <= left_i, pick_i, right_i, put_i <= 1000

"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/time-to-cross-a-bridge/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

2532. Time to Cross a Bridge

There are k workers who want to move n boxes from the right (old) warehouse to the left (new) warehouse. You are given the two integers n and k, and a 2D integer array time of size k x 4 where time[i] = [right_i, pick_i, left_i, put_i].

The warehouses are separated by a river and connected by a bridge. Initially, all k workers are waiting on the left side of the bridge. To move the boxes, the i-th worker can do the following:

- Cross the bridge to the right side in right_i minutes.
- Pick a box from the right warehouse in pick_i minutes.
- Cross the bridge to the left side in left_i minutes.
- Put the box into the left warehouse in put_i minutes.

The i-th worker is less efficient than the j-th worker if either condition is met:
- left_i + right_i > left_j + right_j
- left_i + right_i == left_j + right_j and i > j

The following rules regulate the movement of the workers through the bridge:
- Only one worker can use the bridge at a time.
- When the bridge is unused prioritize the least efficient worker (who have picked up the box) on the right side to cross. If not, prioritize the least efficient worker on the left side to cross.
- If enough workers have already been dispatched from the left side to pick up all the remaining boxes, no more workers will be sent from the left side.

Return the elapsed minutes at which the last box reaches the left side of the bridge.

Example 1:

Input: n = 1, k = 3, time = [[1,1,2,1],[1,1,3,1],[1,1,4,1]]
Output: 6
Explanation:
From 0 to 1 minutes: worker 2 crosses the bridge to the right.
From 1 to 2 minutes: worker 2 picks up a box from the right warehouse.
From 2 to 6 minutes: worker 2 crosses the bridge to the left.
From 6 to 7 minutes: worker 2 puts a box at the left warehouse.
The whole process ends after 7 minutes. We return 6 because the problem asks for the instance of time at which the last worker reaches the left side of the bridge.

Example 2:

Input: n = 3, k = 2, time = [[1,5,1,8],[10,10,10,10]]
Output: 37
Explanation:
The last box reaches the left side at 37 seconds. Notice, how we do not put the last boxes down, as that would take more time, and they are already on the left with the workers.

Constraints:

    1 <= n, k <= 10^4
    time.length == k
    time[i].length == 4
    1 <= left_i, pick_i, right_i, put_i <= 1000
"""


class Solution:
    def findCrossingTime(self, n: int, k: int, time: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        # Heaps provided as builtins: heapify, heappush, heappop
        # left_wait/right_wait: min-heaps with key (-(left+right), -i, i) so popping gives least efficient (largest sum, largest index)
        left_wait = []
        right_wait = []
        left_busy = []  # (free_time, i)
        right_busy = []  # (free_time, i)

        # initialize left_wait with all workers at time 0
        for i in range(k):
            lr = time[i][2] + time[i][0]  # left_i + right_i
            left_wait.append((-(lr), -i, i))
        heapify(left_wait)

        t = 0
        sent = 0  # number of workers dispatched from left to pick (left->right starts)
        transported = (
            0  # number of boxes that have been brought back to left (cross finished)
        )
        last_cross_time = 0

        while transported < n:
            # move finished busy workers to waits if their free_time <= t
            while left_busy and left_busy[0][0] <= t:
                ft, i = heappop(left_busy)
                lr = time[i][2] + time[i][0]
                heappush(left_wait, (-(lr), -i, i))
            while right_busy and right_busy[0][0] <= t:
                ft, i = heappop(right_busy)
                lr = time[i][2] + time[i][0]
                heappush(right_wait, (-(lr), -i, i))

            if right_wait:
                # prioritize least efficient on right to cross to left with a box
                _, _, i = heappop(right_wait)
                # start crossing from right to left at time t
                t += time[i][2]  # left_i
                transported += 1
                last_cross_time = t
                # after crossing, worker will put the box and be busy on left until t + put_i
                heappush(left_busy, (t + time[i][3], i))
            elif left_wait and sent < n:
                # send least efficient on left to go pick a box (left -> right)
                _, _, i = heappop(left_wait)
                # start crossing left to right at time t
                t += time[i][0]  # right_i
                # after crossing, will pick a box and be busy on right until t + pick_i
                heappush(right_busy, (t + time[i][1], i))
                sent += 1
            else:
                # No one can cross now; advance time to next worker finishing a task
                next_times = []
                if left_busy:
                    next_times.append(left_busy[0][0])
                if right_busy:
                    next_times.append(right_busy[0][0])
                if not next_times:
                    # nothing left to do (shouldn't happen in valid inputs)
                    break
                t = min(next_times)

        return last_cross_time


sol = Solution()

print(sol.findCrossingTime(1, 3, [[1, 1, 2, 1], [1, 1, 3, 1], [1, 1, 4, 1]]))  # 6

assert sol.findCrossingTime(1, 3, [[1, 1, 2, 1], [1, 1, 3, 1], [1, 1, 4, 1]]) == 6
assert sol.findCrossingTime(3, 2, [[1, 5, 1, 8], [10, 10, 10, 10]]) == 37

assert sol.findCrossingTime(1, 1, [[1, 1, 1, 1]]) == 3
assert sol.findCrossingTime(1, 5, [[1, 1, 1, 1]] * 5) == 3
assert sol.findCrossingTime(10000, 1, [[1, 1, 1, 1]]) == 39999
assert sol.findCrossingTime(2, 2, [[1000, 1000, 1000, 1000]] * 2) == 4000
assert sol.findCrossingTime(2, 2, [[1, 1, 4, 1], [2, 1, 3, 1]]) == 10
assert sol.findCrossingTime(2, 2, [[1, 1, -1, 1], [1, 1, 1, 1]]) == 2
assert (
    sol.findCrossingTime(
        3, 10, [[i % 3 + 1, i % 5 + 1, i % 7 + 1, i % 11 + 1] for i in range(10)]
    )
    == 27
)
assert sol.findCrossingTime(5, 3, [[1, 1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1, 1], [10, 10, 10, 10]]) == 30
assert sol.findCrossingTime(2, 1, [[1000, 1000, 1000, 1000]]) == 7000
assert (
    sol.findCrossingTime(4, 4, [[1, 1, 4, 1], [2, 1, 3, 1], [3, 1, 2, 1], [4, 1, 1, 1]])
    == 20
)
